श्रीदुंढिराजादिषरूपं नारायणा गणपतिथ्यो नमः ॥ ओ॥ अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजं । होतारं रत्नधाततम्। अग्निः पूर्वेभिर्ऋषिभिरीडो नूनैरुतोलस देवॉ एह वक्षति॥ अग्निना रयिमश्नवत्पोषमेव दिवे दिवे। यशसंवीरवत्। अग्नेय्यज्मं चंख्विभृतः परिसरसि॥ स इदेवेषुगच्छति। अग्निं होतारं कविं क्रतुः सत्यश्चिथश्रवस्तमः। दिवोदेवेभिरागमत्॥१॥ यदुंगराथुपेलमग्नेभद्रेकरिष्यसि। तवेत्तत्सत्यमंगिरः। उपत्वाग्ने दिवेदिवेदोषावस्तर्धियावयम्॥ नमोभरंतमसिराजंतमध्वराणांगोपाभृतस्यदीदिविं। वर्धमानस्खे दमोसनः पितेवसुनवेग्ने सूपायानोनर्शवासुस्वसा नःखस्तये॥२॥ वायवाय्याहिद्रशेत मेसोमा अरंकृतः। तेशापा हि श्रुधी हवीवाय

gemini.text:
We see the shelter of Mitra and Varuna, wide-striding, heroic, and uninjured. Three earths do they uphold, and three heavens, and three are their ordinances that encompass these things. By sacred law, O Adityas, great is that mighty power of yours; Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuna, I praise it.

Three celestial, golden, pure, and purified lights do they sustain. Unconquered, unblinkers, undeceived, widely praised, they protect the mortal with their swiftness.

Thou, O Varuna, art the king of all, of the gods and of mortals, like an Asura. Grant us the radiance of royal splendor, and prolong our lives for the days that lie before us.

Neither by the right hand nor by the left do they go astray, nor towards the east, nor towards the west, nor downward, nor upward. Wise and knowing, through their insight and steadfast ordinance, they bring forth a safe and luminous refuge for them.

O King, he who brings ruin to the wicked, or he who grows strong in battle, or the steadfast ones—abundant wealth goes to him first, accompanied by horses, and he becomes truly praised as one who has offered worship.

Pure, with waters, with good pasture, and with auspicious dwellings, radiant and rich in heroes, he dwells secure. Neither by theft nor by violence, nor from afar, does ruin come upon those who are in the guidance of the Adityas.

No. 9:
Salutations to Sri Huntiraja and the fifty-six rulers! Om! I praise Agni, the domestic priest of the sacrifice, the divine minister, the invoker, and the best bearer of jewels. May this Agni bring hither the gods, who are praised by ancient and modern seers. Through Agni may one attain wealth, and daily increase in nourishment, possessing glory and valiant heroes. O Agni, you encompass on all sides the sacrifice which is without obstruction; indeed, that goes to the gods. Agni is the invoker, wise in will, true, most rich in wondrous fame; may he come hither with the gods from heaven. If one asks: "Should a physician refrain from treating those with deformed or severely altered bodies?"—the answer is no; one should not turn away from them simply because of their appearance. Exhausted by desires, plagued by poisons, or born with congenital defects, such individuals are patients all the same. 

Just as a forest fire is balanced by water, or fierce heat by cooling measures, so too are the bodily humors managed through their opposites. The digestive fire (koshtgni) of such individuals may be fierce, mild, or variable, compounded by poisons, artificial toxins (garavisha), or parasitic worms. 

When the constitutions (prakritis) are afflicted in this manner, along with depleted or deranged bodily elements (dhatus), the physician should determine the treatment based on the specific imbalance of wind, bile, and phlegm, as well as the seasonal changes, the state of digestion, and the patient's strength. 

The bodily elements—chyle (rasa), blood (rakta), flesh (mamsa), fat (medas), bone (asthi), marrow (majja), and semen (shukra)—along with their waste products (malas) such as urine, feces, and sweat, are sustained and nourished in a balanced state. An increase in all of these occurs through similar balancing factors, while a decrease occurs through the opposite. 

The six tastes are sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, and astringent. They reside in various substances and act accordingly to nourish or deplete the body, just as taught in the ancient medical treatises. Therefore, the wise physician should understand these principles thoroughly.

Tapas (austerity), Svadhyaya (study of sacred texts), and Ishvara-pranidhana (surrender to the Supreme Lord) constitute Kriya Yoga. 

Yoga does not succeed through mere austerity by one who is afflicted. Without the piercing power of austerity, the beginningless accumulation of karma-vasanas (subconscious impressions), which are variegated, intensely painful, and entangled in the net of worldly objects, cannot be purified. By undertaking austerity, the pacification of the mind is achieved without obstruction; therefore, this is considered worthy of practice. Svadhyaya is the repetition of sacred mantras such as Om, or the study of scriptures on liberation. Ishvara-pranidhana is the dedication of all actions and the surrender of their fruits to the Supreme Guru. 

This Kriya Yoga is to be practiced for the purpose of bringing about samadhi and for attenuating the kleshas (afflictions).

Verily, this is Kriya Yoga, which serves the purpose of fostering meditative absorption (samadhi) and bringing about the attenuation of mental afflictions (klechas), and it ought to be practiced.

॥ Salutation to Sri Ganesha ॥
Glory to Angarani, who grants the desires of the virtuous, the abode of all splendor, who dwells in the ocean of nectar, who is born of the ocean, who is the embodiment of thirst, the beloved of the enemy of Mada (Indra), to Indira, I offer my salutations. 1. 

By which the spots of the body of the enemy of Utha (Kama) are conquered, and by whose touch a man experiences supreme bliss through the mantra of the nadis. 2. 

Therein, first, the examination of the nadis: When a man's sight is deluded by the intense worldly objects, the nadi of life (jivanadi) is revealed, manifesting its true nature to the eye, encompassing the whole universe in a pair of united eyes. 3. 

Now, the nadi: In the lower abdomen resides [the nadi]; in the middle of it is situated a certain [nadi] known as the Jivanadi, declared by those who know the truth of the nadis. 4. 

Furthermore, by a special piercing at the root of the thumb, extending up to the heart, it pervades everywhere; thus is the origin of the nadi declared by the wise. 5. 

Leaving aside one finger, towards the upper side from the root of the thumb, it is to be known by the wise; this [knowledge] is attained only through practice. 6. 

That which is the pulsing artery (dhamani) at the root of the thumb, known as the Jiva, is firmly established there. For the alleviation of sorrow and for the benefit of women and physicians, this has been diligently composed by me with effort.

gemini.text:
Milk from a cow that drinks warm water becomes heavy and difficult to digest. The milk of a white cow increases kapha, pacifies vata in those whose blood is pure, and cures vata. The milk of a red cow pacifies vata and pitta, is heavy, and cures vata. The milk of a black cow pacifies vata and pitta, and is heavy. The milk of a tawny (shyama) cow alleviates vata and is beneficial for overcoming fluid retention and worms. 

For a person who is extremely emaciated, suffering from chronic fever, blood disorders, dryness, loss of appetite, various diseases, and indigestion, milk is prescribed as highly beneficial. It pacifies kapha, vata, and pitta, promotes clarity and upward movement, destroys emaciation, increases strength, and builds vigor. 

Curd is unctuous, binding (grahi), sour, and hot; it increases kapha and pitta, and is heavy. Curd derived from human milk is beneficial, sour, and superior. Curd prepared from sheep's milk aggravates the doshas and causes obstruction. Fresh curd is beneficial for conditions involving rhinitis, nasal congestion, and loss of appetite.

gemini.text:
Salutation to Sri Ganesha. May he be victorious—the minister of kings, whose form shines like the moon, who is renowned among the learned as the embodiment of the renewal of life, who is the creator, preserver, and destroyer of the worlds, and whose speech is known as the supreme light radiant with the multitude of rays of the letter-symbols. 

1. Having repeatedly examined this science in various scriptures with the aid of astute intellectuals and masters profoundly versed in horoscopy, and wishing to compose a comprehensive work with diverse meters for the delight of the learned and those who understand the true essence of knowledge, I now undertake this task. 2.

Some scholars desire the division of day and night under the name of *Hora*, while others consider karma-earned destiny to always be the true instrument of manifestation. 3.

[Describing bodily limbs corresponding to the signs:] The head, the face, the neck, the chest, the heart, the belly, the pelvis, the loins, the thighs, the knees, the shins, and the feet—these are assigned in order to the twelve signs starting from Aries. 4.

[Description of the zodiacal signs:] Aries is like a ram; Taurus like a bull; Gemini like a human couple with a mace and lute; Cancer like a crab; Leo like a lion; Virgo like a virgin in a boat holding fire and grain; Libra like a man holding a balance; Scorpio like a scorpion; Sagittarius like a centaur with a bow and a horse's lower body; Capricorn like a crocodile and deer; Aquarius like a man holding a water pot; and Pisces like two fish facing each other. 5.

The lords of the signs, starting from Aries, are Mars, Venus, Mercury, the Moon, the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Saturn, and Jupiter. 6.

[Planetary components and relationships:] Mars, the Sun, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are the lords of the bounds (navamshas/drekkanas), followed by... When situated in reverse order from the sign of the Moon and Scorpio, they dwell at the junctions of the constellations. 7.

Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces... 8.

The drekkana, hora, navamsha, saptamsha, trimshamsha... and the field (kshetra)...

tiered_pipeline.text:
Salutations to Sri Ganesha. 

May the moon-crested Lord, radiant in form, who is the support of the universe and the cause of repeated births, be victorious. He who is known as the supreme Brahman—the creator, preserver, and destroyer of the worlds—and whose speech is embodied in the sacred syllables, shines forth like a lamp amidst a cluster of trembling rays. 

Having carefully examined this by means of profound intellect, and having seen it repeatedly set forth in various scriptures by great masters of horoscopy, and wishing to make it fully manifest for the wise through diverse meters and rich meanings in this treatise on the science of time (Hora), some authorities desire the division of day and night according to the sequence of past and future karma, thus rendering it ever manifest. 

[Regarding the bodily forms of the zodiacal signs]: Aries is like a ram; Taurus resembles a bull; Gemini consists of a man and a woman holding a club and a lute; Cancer is like a crab; Leo is like a lion; Virgo is a virgin sitting in a boat holding a cornfield and a fire; Libra is a man holding a balance; Scorpio is like a scorpion; Sagittarius is a centaur with the body of a horse and a human torso holding a bow; Capricorn has the face of a deer and the body of a crocodile (makara); Aquarius is a man holding a water-pot; and Pisces resembles a pair of fish. 

The planetary rulers of the signs [from Aries onwards] are Mars, Venus, Mercury, the Moon, the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Saturn, and Jupiter. Their sub-rulers, planetary periods, aspects, decans, navamshas, saptamshas, trimshamshas, and other divisional charts are thus established according to traditional astrological science.

gemini.text: When the seven-fold division of the apta (or planet) constitutes the hora, and the rising sign (lagna) is divided into two equal parts, [9] the Taurus, Aries, Capricorn, Cancer, and Pisces signs are known by the names of quadrupeds and the like (shara), while Gemini and the others are similarly designated as possessing human forms (sirshyadayah) with two, three, or four legs arising respectively; the remainder are situated on both sides, and odd signs are masculine, [10] while cruel and benefic planets are described in terms of male characteristics; the zodiacal signs represent limbs, with Aries, Taurus, and Cancer together with their triangles corresponding to villages and the like; the mothers, enemies, Indra, Agni, and Brahma correspond to the decans of the moon and others, while the lords of the houses, sons, and trines are established [11]—though some authorities maintain that the first hora is desired by those who desire gain, while others designate the second decan as belonging to the tenth, twelfth, and eleventh signs [12]. Here, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, and Pisces are the daytime risings of the sun and others, while the thirty parts (trimsamsa) are measured by ten, crests, fourteen, sixteen, and eleven [13]. The divisional charts (vargas) in successive order, beginning with the odd and even signs up to the final ones, are known by the names of navamsas yielding auspicious results, while Leo, Taurus, the first [part], Aries, Libra, Aquarius, and Scorpio become signs yielding prosperity [14]. The houses starting from the hora represent the physical body, family, siblings, relatives, children, enemies, spouse, death, fortune, and profession respectively, while the upachayas, dusthanas, and houses of gain and loss are briefly stated by some authorities as being constant [15]. Valour, house, intelligence, and enemies are variously named as the hidden, preceptor, death, expenditure, gains, fourth, and 7th houses, while the fourth, seventh, and tenth constitute the angles (kântaka/kendra), [16] among which—when properly marked—the insect, human, aquatic, and quadruped signs possess strength [17]. Following this sequence mutually, one should understand all the traditional pronouncements regarding the face and mouth, the seventh house (jamitra), the ninth, fifth, and trine houses, the tenth house, and the sign of Cancer [18]. The horas, together with those aspected by Jupiter and other planets...

tiered_pipeline.text: Or else, the sevenfold division starting from the *aptas* is called *hora*. The ascendant becomes [calculated] by taking half of that. The signs [associated with these] in Taurus, Aries, Sagittarius, Capricorn, and Cancer are known as *samūga*, *anīga*, and *śārākhya*. Thus have the wise declared them. Starting from the head, two, three, and one [divisions] respectively arise. The remainder [is distributed likewise], and thus the limbs [are formed] uniformly on both sides. The even [signs] are female, the odd are male, described as movable, fixed, and dual, possessing the bodies of signs. Villages and the like [correspond to them]; Aries, Taurus, and Cancer, along with their trines, [are associated with] mothers, enemies, serpents, fire, and water. The *horā*, *drekkāṇa*, and others [are determined] from the asterisms and the moon. Some maintain that the first *horā* belongs to those desiring splendor, while the second *drekkāṇa* belongs to those of the eleventh and twelfth houses. Here, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, and Scorpio are strong by day when occupied by the sun and other [planets]. The *triṃśāṃśa* [divisions] consist of three, five, eleven, eight, and seven [degrees] for odd signs, and conversely for even signs, bringing auspicious results, known as the *navabhāga* [or *navāṃśa*]. Leo, Taurus, [and others] in their initial portions become [bearers of] wealth and happiness. The *horā* and other [divisions] beginning from the ascendant [represent] the body, family, siblings, relatives, children, enemies, spouse, death, and fortune, shining brightly. The sixth, third, tenth, and eleventh [houses] are the *upacayāni* (growing houses); the enemy, death, and gain [houses] are known as *duḥsthikā* (difficult houses). Some always consider the hidden planets variously. The eighth, ninth, and twelfth [houses] relate to acquisition, fortune, and expenditure. The fourth, seventh, and eighth [houses] are known as *caturasra*, *samastha*, *dyuna*, and the seventh house is [also called] *daṃśa*. The fourth, seventh, and tenth [houses] are designated as *kaṇṭaka*, *kendra*, and *catuṣṭaya*, along with the seventh and the ascendant. Among them, as indicated, [some signs are] strong, [representing] insects, human beings, water-dwellers, and quadrupeds, as traditionally handed down through successive teachings. [Knowing] the seventh house as *jāmitra*, *astabha*, and so forth, one should know the fifth and ninth as *trikoṇa*, and the tenth as *karma*. Thus, the *horā* and other divisions, when aspected by or conjoined with Jupiter and others, [yield their results].

gemini.text:
When the sevenfold divisional charts beginning with the Hora are established in their respective houses, they are declared to be pure. The planets, starting from the Sun, in their proper order, rule over the signs beginning with Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer. These same signs, repeated in the same order, constitute the nine divisions known as the Navamsha. The remainder becomes the ascendant, flanked equally on both sides by these. In these, a pair is formed.

Cruel and benefic planets, masculine and feminine natures, movable, fixed, and dual signs, parts of the body—Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer—along with their trines, constitute the measures of the Hora, Drekkana, Navamsha, and Dwadashamsha, corresponding to their own lords and the lords of the trines.

Some authorities desire the first Hora to be based on the odd signs and the second on the even signs, while they proclaim the Drekkana divisions to be derived from the twelfth and eleventh signs respectively.

The highest exaltation points of the luminaries and planets are respectively: the Sun in Aries, the Moon in Taurus, Mars in Capricorn, Mercury in Virgo, Jupiter in Cancer, Venus in Pisces, and Saturn in Libra. The descending nodes and boundaries of their falls are situated in the exact opposite degrees.

The divisional charts in order—beginning with the odd and even signs, running from the beginning to the middle and the end—are designated as the Navamshas yielding auspicious results. Leo, Taurus, the first part of Sagittarius, and Aquarius are known as the fixed biped signs by nature.

The houses beginning with the ascendant signify the body, family, siblings, relatives, children, enemies, spouse, death, fortune, profession, gains, and losses respectively. The dusthanas, upachayas, trikonas, and quadrants are designated by the wise for the planets.

The houses of the planetary lords in order are: the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth. The fourth, seventh, and tenth houses from the ascendant are known as the quadrants and centers. Among these, when marked by appropriate signs, they represent aquatic, human, water-dwelling, and quadrupedal beings.

From the first house onwards, mutually in succession, they represent the pillars and the entire field of combat. The face, the mouth, and others are understood in their proper sequence in the houses along with the trines, culminating in the tenth house of the zodiac.

Those Horas which are aspected by or conjoined with Jupiter and Mercury bestow auspiciousness.

tiered_pipeline.text: When the seven planets occupy odd signs, or when the Hora falls in a masculine sign, those pure planetary spheres, moving in straight courses, are designated as odd. Conversely, when they occupy even signs, they are called even. These very signs, counted from Aries, are spoken of as the limbs of the cosmic body in sequential order, with the first sign corresponding to the head, and the remaining signs distributed across the body up to the ascendant, equally on both sides. Among these, the masculine, feminine, and dual signs, as well as movable, fixed, and dual signs, are described as embodying the physical forms of the planets. Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer, along with their trines, represent the primary categories. Some authorities maintain that the first Hora of an odd sign belongs to the Sun, while others assign the second Hora of the sign of the lord of gains to the decanate. The twelfth and eleventh signs, originating from the unseen aspect of Capricorn and Cancer, are associated with the Sun and other luminaries, reaching their exaltation points. The degrees of the decanates, starting from Aries and extending through Taurus, Gemini, and the rest, up to the final degrees, yield auspicious results known as Navamshas. Leo, Taurus, the first part of Sagittarius, and Libra and Aquarius constitute the trinal houses without doubt. The houses beginning from the ascendant represent the body, family, siblings, relatives, children, enemies, spouse, death, fortune, profession, gains, and losses respectively. The dusthana houses, upachayas, and other functional divisions are assigned by sages to the various planets systematically. The fourth, seventh, and tenth houses are designated as the angles or quadrants. The lords of the seventh, first, fourth, and tenth houses, when suitably marked, bestow strength. Insect, human, water-dwelling, and quadruped signs follow one another in succession. All warfare and worldly struggles, the face of the earth, and the subterranean realms are to be understood within the wheel of the zodiac according to their proper order in the houses, starting from the first and extending through the trines and the tenth sign. The Horas thus viewed, when aspected by Jupiter and Mercury, confer auspiciousness.

gemini.text:
Salutation to Sri. Ah 1.
Obeisance to Lord Ganesha. Obeisance to Lord Purushottama. Obeisance to [Sri Kirtana and others].
[Addressing the Supreme Being who destroys the bondage of worldly existence and is worshipped by Uma and others...]
...Salutation to that Supreme Being who is the physician for all diseases such as attachment, the dispeller of delusion, and the bestower of knowledge and devotion.
Now, we shall expound the science of medicine as desired, for the fulfillment of the primary goals of life (dharma, artha, kama, and moksha). Thus spoke the great sages, led by Atreya: For one who desires long life, the pursuit of righteousness (dharma), wealth (artha), and the means of attaining them (sukha), utmost reverence should be paid to the teachings of Ayurveda. Brahma remembered the Veda of life; from Him it passed to Prajapati, from Prajapati to the Ashvins, and from them to Indra, who bestowed it upon the sages (such as Atreya and others) to dispel the afflictions of beings suffering from diseases. 
Thus, for the benefit of humanity afflicted by various ailments, the science is set forth comprehensively. It comprises eight branches: Internal Medicine (Kayachikitsa), Pediatrics (Bala), Psychiatry/Demonology (Graha), Surgery (Urdhvanga/Shalakya), Toxicology (Damstra/Agada), Rejuvenation (Jara/Rasayana), and Virility/Aphrodisiacs (Vrishya/Vajikarana). 
In brief, the humors (doshas) that govern the body are three: Vata (Wind), Pitta (Bile), and Kapha (Phlegm).

pipeline_records.translation:
Shri!

May we attain the wide, heroic, and inviolable shelter of Mitra and Varuna. Three earths do they uphold, and three heavens; three are the divine laws that govern the inner spaces. By cosmic order (Ṛta), O Aditya, great is your majesty, and great is that supreme dominion which Mitra and Varuna maintain.

The three golden, luminous, and pure celestial realms they uphold, pure and purified by duty. Unconquered, sleepless, and unhurt, they grant abundant praise to the mortal.

You, O Varuna, are the king of all, of gods and of mortals alike. Grant us a hundred paths and dispel our sleeplessness; lengthen our lives, as you did for the ancients.

You do not fail to discern the right from the left, nor the ancient from the recent, nor do you wander from the path, O purifier. The ignorant man, the wise, the hero, and the eloquent all reach your fearless light.

That king who unfailingly bestows bountiful wealth upon the pious—he whose ever-growing prosperity is sustained—that wealthy man moves forward first with his chariot, knowing the earth and bestowing abundance.

Blessed with pure waters, good pasture, and auspicious fortune, growing ever wider, rich in heroes—no one falls into bondage, nor strays afar, when guided by the Adityas.
pipeline_records.explanation: The text prays to the deities Mitra and Varuna for shelter, stating that they uphold three earths, three heavens, and divine laws. It describes Varuna as the king of all gods and mortals, and asks him to grant long life, dispel sleeplessness, and provide safe paths. Finally, it states that those guided by the Adityas receive abundant wealth, good pastures, and freedom from bondage.

pipeline_records.translation:
Salutation to Sri Dundhiraja. Salutation to Ganesha. Om. 

I praise Agni, the household priest of the sacrifice, the divine minister, the hotar priest, who bestows the greatest wealth. Agni, worthy of praise by ancient and modern seers, may he bring the gods here. Through Agni, one obtains wealth, day by day increasing, prosperous, and abounding in heroes. O Agni, whatever sacrifice and ritual you encompass on all sides, that truly reaches the gods. Agni the hotar, the wise poet, true in his works, possessing the most glorious fame, may he arrive with the gods. 

Whatever auspicious deed you, O Agni, will do for the pious worshipper, that truth belongs to you alone, O Angiras. Day by day, O Agni, we approach you with our thoughts, O burner in the night, bringing homage to you who shine as king of sacrifices, guardian of the cosmic order, radiant in your own abode. O Agni, be easy of access to us, like a father to his son; abide with us for our well-being. 

Come, O Vayu, for you are a welcome sight; these Soma juices have been prepared. Drink of them, hear our call.
pipeline_records.explanation: The text begins with salutations to Sri Dundhiraja and Ganesha, followed by praises to the fire god Agni as a priest, provider of wealth, and bringer of the gods to sacrifices. Worshippers offer homage to Agni, asking him to accept their prayers, protect the cosmic order, and be easily accessible to them like a father to his son. Finally, the passage calls upon Vayu to come and drink the prepared Soma juices after hearing the call.

pipeline_records.translation:
Salutation. 
Salutation to Lord Ganesha. Salutation to Lord Purushottama. 

[Invocation and praise to the Supreme Lord/Deities for the removal of worldly bondage and ignorance, and for the attainment of knowledge and liberation.]

Now, we shall expound the chapter known as the "Desire for Longevity" (Āyushkāmīya). Therefore, those who desire longevity should apply the utmost respect to the teachings of Ayurveda (the science of life). 

Brahman remembered this science of life (Ayurveda); from Him, Prajapati [learned it]; from Prajapati, the Ashvins [learned it]; and from them, [Indra, the lord of gods, learned it]. From them, Agnivesha and other [sages learned it]; and they [sub-divided it] into five branches. 

[Considering that] people are generally afflicted by various subjects and possess short lifespans and weak intellects, [this concise essence] is composed for their easy comprehension. 

[Ayurveda] comprises eight branches: 
1. Internal Medicine (Kāya-chikitsā)
2. Pediatrics (Bāla-roga/Kaumāra-bhṛtya)
3. Psychiatry/Demonic Afflictions (Graha-chikitsā)
4. Treatment of Diseases above the Clavicle/ENT (Ūrdhvāṅga-chikitsā or Śālākya-tantra)
5. Surgery (Śalya-tantra)
6. Toxicology (Daṁṣṭrā-chikitsā or Agada-tantra)
7. Rejuvenation (Jarā-chikitsā or Rasāyana-tantra)
8. Aphrodisiacs (Vṛṣya-chikitsā or Vājīkaraṇa)

The humors (doshas), in brief, are three: Vata (Wind), Pitta (Bile), and Kapha (Phlegm).
pipeline_records.explanation: The text begins with salutations to deities and introduces the upcoming chapter called "Desire for Longevity," noting that the teachings of Ayurveda should be followed by those wanting a long life. It outlines the lineage of how Ayurveda was passed down from Brahman through various figures to sages who divided it into five branches. Finally, it lists the eight branches of Ayurveda and states that the three bodily humors are Vata, Pitta, and Kapha.

pipeline_records.translation:
If one should ask: "How should one live, keeping oneself unaffected amidst both altered and unaltered states of the body?"—the response is given: through the avoidance of such things [harmful items/influences] just as one avoids poison. 

The syllable 'ra' combined with 'o', 'ma', 'dho', and 'rdha' belongs to the breath and upper channels. Regarding the stages of age, days, nights, and consumed food—these beginning with the middle ones constitute the state of *kru*. 

Through mothers and them, those who are afflicted by poison, possessing a dull *mandrāgni* (digestive fire), and balanced by equals, have a balanced gastric fire (*koṣṭha*), [residing in] regions like Kuru and Maru. 

By means of *ime*, *yoṣā*, *ambasthā*, and others, even when equal, the one whose birth is marked by *visela*, *vavi*, and the secretion of worms—their intrinsic natures (*prakṛti*) are such that their middle [portion] is emaciated, and their upper part is prominent. They are distinct, having balanced *dhātus* (tissues). 

Likewise, [those characterized by] *śuniyādi*, *toṣattā*, *tajjñā*, *tolangula*, being cold—such a person [suffers from] the seven root-winds (or *mūlānila*). In bile and flesh, there is excessive *go*, *sela*, *nuvi*, and the accumulation of phlegm (*sema-saṁsdavam*). 

Oily, cold, heavy, of fat, stout, red, steady—such is phlegm (*kapha*), along with heat, perspiration, urine, and feces. From the aggravation of that pair [doshas], the seven *dhātus* (tissues)—chyle (*rasa*), blood (*asṛk*), flesh (*māṁsa*), fat (*medas*), bone (*asthi*), marrow (*majjā*), and semen (*śukra*)—along with waste products (*mala*), urine, semen, and *kṣeṭa*, are maintained. Their increase is brought about by things that are similar, and their decrease by things that are opposite. 

The tastes (*rasa*) are sweet (*svādu*), sour (*amla*), salty (*lavaṇa*), bitter (*tikta*), pungent (*uṣṇa/kaṭu*), and astringent (*kaṣāyaka*). Relying upon the stomach (*āmāśaya*), they are [known] thus; by them strength and weakness are [determined]. Among these, the first is understood to be *māruta* (wind).
pipeline_records.explanation: One should live by avoiding harmful influences just as one avoids poison to remain unaffected by changes in the body. The text lists various physical elements, bodily humors like phlegm and bile, the seven bodily tissues, and bodily wastes, noting that similar substances increase them while opposite substances decrease them. Finally, it identifies the six tastes—sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, and astringent—which reside in the stomach and determine strength and weakness, with the first being wind (*māruta*).

pipeline_records.translation: Generally, markers such as gender and others aggravate kapha and kashaya (astringent), while in due order pitta and vata are pacified. A substance is known in three ways according to pacification, provocation, or being unchanged. Potency (virya) is twofold (hot and cold) or threefold based on the predominance of qualities, and also threefold in vipaka (post-digestive effect), being sweet, sour, or pungent in nature. The qualities (gunas) are twenty, starting with heavy, soft, cold, unctuous, smooth, hot, and stable. Through the permutations of time, substance, action, and combinations, they become threefold. When properly applied, these are the causes of health; their imbalance is the cause of disease. Disease is the imbalance of the doshas, and the equilibrium of the doshas is health. Diseases are traditionally classified as endogenous (nija) and exogenous (agantuja). Treatment is also twofold: physical and mental. Rajas and tamas are the mental doshas. Examination of patients should be conducted by means of interrogation, observation, and palpation. Disease is understood through its origin, premonitory symptoms, actual symptoms, and the attainment of relief through therapeutic measures. Knowledge is twofold by nature. Because it arises from vitiated kapha and other doshas, the region of water is characterized by common and balanced impurities in a threefold manner.
pipeline_records.explanation: This passage explains the effects of substances on bodily doshas, the properties of potency and qualities, and how balance defines health while imbalance causes disease. Diseases are classified as endogenous or exogenous, with mental doshas identified as rajas and tamas, and patients are examined through interrogation, observation, and palpation. Finally, diseases are understood through their origin, symptoms, and relief, while treatment is divided into physical and mental methods.

pipeline_records.translation:
From the beginning of Shravishtha, the sun and moon turn northward. The southern course of the sun occurs in Magha. Thus, the solstices are always in Shravishtha and Magha. 

Righteousness and water increase, water springs forth, and the nights become shorter when the course is northward; when it is southward, the reverse is true. The shift of the solstices takes place by sixty muhurtas (over the course of the year).

Twice the seventh, or thirteen from the beginning of the ayana (solstice); the fourth, tenth, and likewise from the double pair (twelfth), as known from the rule of the *bahula* (waning phase).

Vasu, Tvashtar, Bhaga, Aryaman, Mitra, Sarpa, Ashvinin, Jala (Varuna), Dhata, Kanthshva (Aryaman/Kuhuh), Adhyayana, Ashva, and the five stars of Abhijit... 

Sixfold parts are to be made, and twelve fortnights have elapsed. Eleven multiplied and diminished... the bright fortnight... on the second or eighth day. 

Parts should be established in the sixfold place, and twenty kalas for time.
pipeline_records.explanation: The text describes the movements of the sun and moon, stating that their northern course begins in Shravishtha and their southern course in Magha. During the northern course, nights become shorter while righteousness, water, and springs increase, with the reverse occurring during the southern course. It also lists specific constellations, numerical calculations for time, solstices, and fortnights, and instructions for dividing parts and measuring time using kalas.

Having thus rendered the afflictions weakened by the fire of discriminative discernment (prasaṁkhyāna)—such that their seed-nature is burned away and they are no longer subject to production—their mere manifestation, no longer touched by coarse afflictions, shines forth as subtle wisdom. Through their attenuation, those [modifications] ultimately resolve back into their source (pratiprasava).

Additionally, it defines deep sleep as a latent state where the mind's seeds remain intact, while awakening is the mind turning toward an object of support.

Salutation to Lord Ganesha. Now begins the second pada (chapter). 

Having explained the yoga of one whose mind is already concentrated, [the text] now begins to answer how yoga is attainable for one whose mind is distracted. 

Austerity, study of sacred texts, and surrender to the supreme Lord constitute Kriya Yoga. Without austerity, yoga cannot succeed. The mind's impurity—consisting of unfulfilled desires, subtle impressions of past actions (vasanas), various intensely painful torments, and entanglement in worldly objects—cannot be completely destroyed without the smelting fire of austerity. 

Therefore, through the practice of austerity, the mind becomes purified and untroubled; thus, it is considered worthy of being practiced. 

"Study" (svadhyaya) means the repetition of purifying mantras such as Om, or the study of scriptures on liberation. 

"Surrender to Isvara" (Ishvara pranidhana) means the dedication of all actions to the supreme Guru, or the renunciation of the fruits of actions. 

This Kriya Yoga is [undertaken] for the purpose of cultivating Samadhi and for attenuating the afflictions (kleshas). Indeed, it is worthy of being practiced by the seeker.
pipeline_records.explanation: This passage explains that Kriya Yoga consists of austerity, the study of sacred texts, and surrender to the supreme Lord, which helps achieve concentration for a distracted mind. Austerity is essential because it acts like a smelting fire to destroy mental impurities, while study involves repeating mantras or reading liberation scriptures, and surrender means dedicating all actions or their fruits to the supreme Guru. Ultimately, this practice is undertaken to cultivate Samadhi and weaken the afflictions.
pipeline_records.keywords: Kriya Yoga, Tapas, Svadhyaya, Ishvara Pranidhana, Klesha, Samadhi

When the expression "atha" is employed in the sense of modification (vikāra) and determination (adhyavasāya), it conveys conjunction, as declared by one who is competent in the authoritative treatise on instruction (anuśāsana-śāstra). 

Now, one might object: just as the maxim of "the half-forest, half-field" applies to a cowherd, does it not apply here to the treatise of Manu? To this, it must be understood that just as the maxim regarding heaviness pertains to yoga, as has been stated—analogous to how water, when associated with a mechanism (yantra) or channel, engages in action, whereas on its own it is not the object of action—so too, when intending to express the agency of the doer, the competency of the authoritative treatise pertains to the domain of yoga. The underlying meaning is that the subject is indeed qualified precisely because it falls within the operational scope of the treatise. 

Moreover, the import of competency regarding what follows—as implied by the terms concerning the embankment and regulation of water—might otherwise generate doubt regarding words and doubt regarding meaning. 

"Yoga" means *samādhi* (meditative absorption). This is derived from the root *yuj* in the sense of *samādhi*, and not from the root *yuj* in the sense of mere conjunction (*saṁyoga*). 

Now, the established text is understood to be: "Yoga is the authoritative treatise on instruction." Yoga is *samādhi*. And that *samādhi* is an attribute of the mind (*cittasya dharma*).
pipeline_records.explanation: The word "atha" conveys conjunction when used to mean modification and determination. The text clarifies that "yoga" means meditative absorption (*samādhi*), which comes from the root *yuj* meaning *samādhi* rather than mere conjunction. Understanding medicine as twofold—consisting of purification and pacification—and following the sequence of bodily knowledge and obstruction, one distinguishes between the superior and inferior. Or, through the purging of bile, emesis, and likewise oil massage, ghee prescribed by physicians, and the nourishment of the eyes, the pacification of the mind and intellect is indeed the supreme medicine. The physician, expert in practice, radiant, and free from arrogance, administers treatment as designated in the medical treatises, observing the fourfold system. The wise physician, devoted to sacred texts and endowed with supreme skill, should swiftly administer the decoction, the paste, the formulation, and the heart-cleansing medicines along with mantra applications. Here, the intelligent practitioner, well-versed in blood-letting and guided by reason, a wise yogi and physician, eliminates the scorching fever even without other primary medicines. Through restraint of the senses and control of the self, one overcomes delusion and similar ailments without complications. The intelligent physician attends to the obstruction of the channels as taught in tradition, utilizing water mixed with milk, treatments involving instruments and other means, regimens of dry fomentation, bathing, vows, and the observance of proper diets, thereby averting the recurrence of disease without deviation.
pipeline_records.explanation: Time, grass, and bodily states do not create medicines, which are instead divided into purification and pacification, allowing a physician to distinguish between superior and inferior treatments. A skilled and humble physician follows medical texts to treat patients using methods such as purging, emesis, oil massage, prescribed ghee, eye nourishment, decoctions, pastes, and mantras. pipeline_records.translation: Or, one may attain stability of the mind through those [exhaling and inhaling]. Or, a sensory-oriented mental activity, when arisen, binds the mind to stability. When one concentrates on the tip of the nose, there arises the perception of divine fragrance, which is the olfactory activity. At the tip of the tongue, the perception of divine taste. On the palate, the perception of form. In the middle of the tongue, the perception of divine touch. At the root of the tongue, the perception of divine sound. These activities, when arisen, bind the mind to stability, dispel doubt, and become gateways to the intuitive wisdom of Samadhi. By this same principle, it should be understood that sensory activities arising in regard to the sun, moon, planets, gems, the flame of a lamp, or other such objects are likewise sensory-oriented (*vishayavati*). Although in those cases the object is understood through scripture, inference, and the instruction of a teacher, and though it becomes fully illuminated by wisdom with the capacity to establish the true nature of things, yet, as long as it is not directly experienced by one's own faculties—even in part—so long, like something indirect, it fails to produce a firm conviction regarding subtle truths such as liberation. Therefore, scripture, inference, and the instruction of a teacher...
pipeline_records.explanation: The mind can achieve stability through exhaling and inhaling, or through sensory-oriented mental activities that arise when concentrating on specific body parts like the nose or tongue. These perceptions stabilize the mind, remove doubt, and lead to the intuitive wisdom of Samadhi, similar to sensory activities experienced with objects like the sun, moon, or gems. However, until these subtle truths are directly experienced by one's own faculties, knowledge gained solely from scriptures, inference, and teachers remains indirect and fails to produce firm conviction.

pipeline_records.translation:
Certainly, a specific special object must be investigated. When a partial aspect of that taught object is investigated, the entire subject matter, even though extremely subtle, is revealed up to the state of liberation (apavarga). For this very purpose, this mental purification (cittaparikarma) is prescribed. When the fluctuating mental modifications (vrittis) are controlled and the designation of mastery (vashikara-samjna) regarding that object arises, he becomes capable of investigating this and that object. That being the case, faith, energy, mindfulness, and concentration will arise for him without obstruction. 

"Or [the meditation that is] sorrowless and luminous, [pertaining to] the Purusha." When such an activity arises, it secures the steadiness of the mind as one focuses it upon the lotus of the heart and perceives the intellect (buddhi). For the intellect indeed possesses a radiant, ether-like nature. There, through proficiency in stability, that very nature [of the intellect] is perceived in the forms of the brilliance of the sun, moon, planets, and jewels. 

And when the mind is absorbed in the sense of 'I-ness' (asmita), it becomes tranquil, infinite, and akin to a motionless great ocean, consisting solely of 'I-ness' alone. Regarding this, it has been said: "Realizing that Self as no larger than an atom, one knows 'I am'."
pipeline_records.explanation: Investigating a specific object reveals even the most subtle subjects up to liberation, which is the purpose of mental purification. When the fluctuating mental activities are controlled and mastery is achieved, a person gains the ability to investigate objects and experiences unobstructed faith, energy, mindfulness, and concentration. Additionally, a sorrowless and luminous meditation focused on the heart secures the steadiness of the mind by revealing the radiant nature of the intellect, eventually leading the mind to absorb into a tranquil, infinite state of pure 'I-ness'.

त्ताश्रूष्ट हवारिय श्रेजलै जलीगू डसंस्पशनं ॥ सर्पिः क्षीरविरेकं रुधिर स्त्रावप्रदेहार्दिकां पानाहारविहार भेभजनमि दं पिंतप्रशान्तिंनयेन ॥ दुरासभापर्यट कपप्रियंगु भूम्यानिसवासाक दुरो हिराणिनां ॥ जलैपिबेच्छर्करार्याचागढ तृष्णानपि ज्वरदार्हयुतः ॥ यक्रिकः ॥ यरोल यवानिः क्वाथोमधुनामधुरी हृतः ॥ तीव्रपित्तज्वरानम्नदीपानाम्नदाहनाशनं
pipeline_records.translation: Physician, for dry conditions, [give] goat meat with *saguropahan* [or appropriate meat soup], not sheep, along with *sasuṣī*, *śārivā*, grapes (*drākṣā*), *śaṇapuṣpī*, and *punarnavā*. For *saguroyambaka*, goat [meat/milk] destroys fever. Grapes and *guḍūcī* together, along with *gāyamānā* [or *gāyatrī*] and black pepper, prepared as a decoction or pills along with *vedan*, destroys fever. [Another formula:] *sājājī* (cumin), *pippalīmūla*, *bhṛṅga*, *vaikarājṛtā*, *abhayā*, *vṛddhamṛdvīkā*... [corrupted/dense manuscript fragment regarding ingredients for tremors and spasms]... destroys *anila* (Vata) fever. Cloves, *mṛtpalkhaṇī*, goat-root (*ajārjāmūla*), ginger (*nāgara*), *pippalī*, *kaṭuka*, *paparī* — these powders or pills made with jaggery constitute a *modaka* that destroys *vātajvara* (Vata fever). [Heading:] Lavangādi [Recipe] for Vātika Jvara: Immediate drinking of ghee is highly praised, as well as milk with sugar, especially mixed with ghee. [Heading:] Drinking of ghee for Vātivajvara. [Heading:] He states the treatment for Pitta: Bitter, astringent, and sweet substances, cool shade, cooling applications... [fragmentary verse on managing burning sensations, thirst, and Pitta fever through appropriate drinks, diet, and lifestyle, blood-letting, and purgation with medicated ghee and milk]. *Durālabhā*, *paryaṭaka*, *priyaṅgu*, *bhūmyāmalakī*, *vāsā*, *durohirāṇi* — these taken with water and sugar quench thirst and alleviate burning fever. pipeline_records.explanation: This text provides specific remedies and treatments for different types of fevers. It lists various herbal mixtures, meats, decoctions, pills, and dietary guidelines—such as consuming ghee and milk—to cure fevers caused by Vata and Pitta conditions, along with symptoms like tremors, burning sensations, and thirst.

pipeline_records.translation:
Potassium carbonate and specifically *suvarcikā* (natron/sodium carbonate): Yavakṣāra (potassium carbonate from barley) is light, unctuous, hot, and digestive; it destroys leprosy, vāta disorders, fat, dyspnea, and throat diseases. [It cures...] and heart ailments. The properties of *sarjikākṣāra* (sodium carbonate): it destroys fluid/lymph-related disorders, phlegm, and abdominal tumors (gulma). *Suvarcikā* and *sarjikā* are beneficial for the eyes and cure various diseases according to the experts. 

Now, regarding *sodarāgā* (borax): Borax, tankana, and related substances are discussed. Tankana alleviates phlegm and vāta, while aggravating pitta. 

The two essences (*sāra-dvaya*): *sarjikā* and *yavakṣāra* are declared to be the pair of essences (*sāra-dvaya*). 

The three essences (*sāra-traya*): When tankana is added to the previous two, it is spoken of as the triad of essences (*sāra-traya*). Combined, that triad of three... destroys... [various ailments]. 

The eight essences (*sāra-aṣṭaka*): [The ashes of] palāśa, vahni (chitraka), śikhari (amaphalā/apāmārga), vi..., arka, and tilanāla (sesame stalks), along with yavakṣāra and sarjikā, are declared to be the eight essences (*sāra-aṣṭaka*). 

Now, regarding *tukkācuka* (or *sukra/tankana* varieties): Sahasravedhi, svādu..., sahasra, also known as śukra. Śukra is extremely hot and digestive... It is a fluid/substance that destroys colic, abdominal tumors (gulma), constipation, rheumatism, phlegm-related ailments... it removes vomiting, pain in the mouth, bodily distress... removes fever and morbid flesh.
pipeline_records.explanation: The text lists various alkaline substances and minerals—such as potassium carbonate, sodium carbonate, borax, and plant ashes—along with their specific combinations called essences. It describes their medicinal uses, stating that they improve digestion, warm the body, and cure ailments like leprosy, phlegm disorders, abdominal tumors, joint pain, and other diseases.
pipeline_records.keywords: Yavakṣāra, Suvarcikā, Tankaṇa, Sāra-traya, Sāra-aṣṭaka, Alkali formulation

pipeline_records.translation: With eyes tawny and venomous, born of nine nodes, well-joined, bitter, and astringent, it is an elixir, beneficial to the complexion, good for the voice, and pungent in digestion, promoting the digestive fire. Previously tormented by Hara and Suraja in bodily form, it is born from the churning of the milk ocean. Guggulu increases flesh, is aphrodisiac, promotes health and longevity, is slimy, unctuous, fragrant, digestive, and pungent, free from the sour and salty tastes. Endowed with these qualities, it promotes muscle growth, increases strength, enhances vision, serves as a healing agent, is beneficial to the heart, and is wholesome against diseases of the healthy. Being bitter, astringent, and slightly sour, it destroys pitta. It heals wounds and growths, destroys worms and urinary disorders. Due to its freshness, it is nourishing, aphrodisiac, destroys old age, and grants strength. The names of Guggulu are: Kumkuma, Ruchaka, Kudai, Simha, Simhi, Gopura, Chura, Khyapura, Tihya, Ganga, Shavela, Nagadhupriya, Sugandha, suitable for fumigation, and useful in anointing practices. Kunduru juice is pungent, destroys kapha, and gladdens the heart. Sallaki juice is called Kunduru, which destroys phlegm disorders. It is known to cure fever, asthma, cough, and colic. Amalavimala, Dhiha, Vajraphena, Rasalika—these are purgative downwards, destroying grass, bush, and poison-induced disorders. It destroys poison, alleviates diseases, and Satala destroys ulcers. Tridhara (Snuhi) is a purgative. Sansini.

Nighantu:

Tahara, bola, sugandha, uttu, nashanah, vo janam, nakhonaga, hanuh, shakti, vadari-patrakah, shapah. Made, dhudhura, karajah, shigrachvanavarasvarah, karuha, machhana, kho bala, prahara, tatha. Ma chandhi, jobbah, shainah, kutasthah, eka-kajakah. 

Sugandhi, kapha-klighna, dhupa-nepenakarmanah, nakha-kshayan-cha ghritaman, varna-rutna-khameva cha. Ma ghunara, khanamah, shree-veshtakah, payasakah, shree-sakorakta, sheerbhakah. Niryasah saralānancha dadikashrakha-budumah. Sugandhi, shvikalah, snigdho, dhuyataila-adhivasanah. 

Shreeveshtakah kapahaharah, pratishayaharah, sarah. Shree-veshtru-nama oomam, bahinkaraktam, pishpoonam, varayo nikamkamiram, stuvaen chamajaya, grisamamtatha. 

Snigdhochcha vata-shamanam, varna-kritu deha-gandha-rutey. Kumkumam rasa-tiktam kashayam krimi-nashanam, unkusha-shankarapramee-re nrisimham. Chanda, dhana-hari, vora, krimika taskaree tatha. 

Nishavari, tiravinee, kayam chika, naushakee, tini, sugandhi deha-yogam mama jana yoga-ksharaani. Vanda labha, kapha-ghree, vadhuta lepanadimih, chanda anna-deyo na mitaka, pungu gola-hiyatashra keethya ko gami-antarah. Mattam baro vanka, maya-ni saduko ra triga punargurum.

It describes their physical qualities—such as being fragrant, oily, or bitter—and states their uses in treating phlegm, colds, worms, and various bodily ailments.

In the secret part of the hand, at the base of the thumb, leaving aside one finger's breadth, by means of piercing with ink, and then pressing downward repeatedly with the fingers, one should examine the pulsations of the subtle channels of the hand, according to the scriptures, tradition, and personal experience, for the attainment of well-being.

In the beginning, within the vital channels carrying the breath, which are blazing like fire, the intelligent practitioner should understand the condition of the pulse through disorders of phlegm. 

In terms of its meaning: when wind (vata) is predominant, the pulse becomes clearly manifest at the base of the index finger; when bile (pitta) is predominant, it is in the middle finger; and when phlegm (kapha) is predominant, it is felt as a globule in the third (ring) finger. When both wind and phlegm are present, it is in the index and middle fingers. When bile is predominant, it is distinctly in the middle and ring fingers. When wind, pitta, and kapha are all present together across the three fingers, the three doshas are to be recognized as conjoined.

The pulse belonging to the wind current is fickle (chapala); the one carrying bile is steady (sthira); the one possessing phlegm is declared to be sluggish and heavy; and the one exhibiting all characteristics possesses speed. Due to phlegm, it is steady and slow; when mixed, it is observed through mixed signs. Thus, the expert should declare the prognostic outcome.
pipeline_records.explanation: To examine the pulse, a practitioner presses a specific spot near the base of the thumb on the hand to feel the subtle channels for well-being. The location and movement of the pulse indicate which bodily humors—wind, bile, or phlegm—are dominant or mixed. Each humor produces distinct physical characteristics in the pulse, allowing an expert to observe these signs and determine the condition.

pipeline_records.translation: The milk of a white cow, when partaken, mitigates Vata and pacifies Pitta, but is productive of Kapha; whereas that of a red cow is beneficial for Vata and Pitta, though dry (rough) and heavy. The milk of a yellow cow alleviates Vata and Kapha, while pacifying Pitta; and that of a dark (black or blue-black) cow is heavy, alleviates Vata, and is beneficial in conditions of emaciation and chronic fever. Curd is oily, astringent, heavy, and tends to increase Kapha and Pitta while promoting strength. Sour curd is superior in increasing semen and strength, but it is slow to digest and causes a burning sensation if consumed at night. Curd is cooling, mitigates Vata, and is excellent for those suffering from emaciation and wasting diseases.
pipeline_records.explanation: The milk of cows with different colors affects the body's humors in specific ways, such as white cow milk mitigating Vata and Pitta while increasing Kapha, and black cow milk helping with emaciation and chronic fever. Curd is oily, heavy, increases Kapha and Pitta, promotes strength, and is cooling. Additionally, sour curd increases semen and strength but digests slowly and causes a burning sensation at night, while general curd helps those suffering from wasting diseases and mitigates Vata.

ृह.जा. १
श्रीगणेशाय नमः। मूर्तिर्विपरिकल्पितः शशभृतो वर्ष्मापुनर्जन्मना-मास्तिक्यात्मविदां क्रतुश्वयजता मन्त्रीमर्डेपतिष्ठां लोकानां प्रलयोद्भवस्थितिभुवः स्थानं विधायः श्रुतोवाचंसः सदशात्मनेककिरणश्रेणे लोसदीपारथिः १ मर्योभिः पटुबुद्धिभिः पटुधियां होराफलज्ञप्रयेष्वदृष्टायसमन्वितेमुवदृशः शस्तेषु दक्षेत्रापि होरातंत्रमहाशीवेप्रतररींभग्नोद्यमानामहंसंसंवृत्तविचित्रमर्थवद्लेशास्त्रज्ञवेद्दारभे २ होरेत्येहोरात्रविकलूपमेकेवांछंतिरवीपरवरशीलोपात्तः कर्माजिर्तार्एवं भवेसदादियन्नस्यपंक्तिंसमभि-व्यक्तं ३ कालींगातिवरंगमाम नृपुरैशलोउवासाभृतोवस्तिव्यंनमूरूजानुयुगले जंघेततौप्रि-दयं मेषाश्चिप्रथमोनवर्षचरणाश्चक्रस्थिता राशयोराशिक्षेत्रगृहरुक्षभानिभवतं चैकार्यसंग्रतयेः ४ मत्योधृटीनुप्रिथुर्नसगदेंवीरांचापीनरोश्च्जघनोमकरोमृगाप्यः तौलीससस्पदहनाप्लावगाव क-न्यांशिखासामसरशाः स्वचरश्चसर्वै ५ क्षितिजसितज्ञनन्दूरवि सोम्सितावनिजाः सुरगुरुसौरिसं-दगुरुवश्चरृहांशकपाः अजमगत्तौलिंवरूभयनादिनवांशविधिर्भवेनसमांशसाधिपतयः सुरग्रहक्र्री-मशः ६ कुजरविगुरुज्ञशुक्रभागाः पयनसमीरणकीर्य्यटजूकालेयाः अय्युजिमुजिंभेंविपर्यय-स्थ्याः शशशिवहनालिऋक्षांतमृक्षसंधि ७ क्रियताबुशिजितमुकीरलेयपाथोमज्मकफोप्यर्माताक्षि-कन्याकोकेशरहशेषगप्मोंसमंचेखं ८ द्रेर्क्काहोरामवेभागसंक्तात्रिंशंकम्यदिरसोशकश्च क्षेत्रंच

pipeline_records.translation:
Salutation to Lord Ganesha. 

The embodied form of the Moon is mentally conceived through the recurrence of births; for the faithful and the knowers of the Self, it is the sacrificial rite; for those who perform sacrifices, it is the minister and the lord of the assembly. Establishing the sustenance, origin, and dissolution of the worlds as its abode, He who is renowned spoke thus: He who possesses a multitude of rays like the soul of the ten directions, the lamp of the world, shining brightly, is comprehended by the wise with sharp intellects. For those of keen understanding who desire to know the results of horoscopy, and who are endowed with unseen fortune, even the skilled in auspicious and efficient fields find their efforts broken in the great ocean of horoscopic science. 

Therefore, I commence this treatise, which is varied, meaningful, rich in scriptural knowledge, and known by the wise. Some desire 'Hora' to be a modification of 'ahoratra' (day and night), derived from the acquisition of actions earned through the nature of the sun and the other planets. Thus, the series of the zodiacal signs (beginning with Aries) manifested in regular order corresponds to the bodily limbs: the head of the cosmic purusha is Aries, Taurus is the face, Gemini the chest, Cancer the heart, Leo the stomach, Virgo the hips, Libra the lower abdomen, Scorpio the genitals, Sagittarius the thighs, Capricorn the two knees, Aquarius the shanks, and Pisces the two feet. 

The terms *rasi*, *kshetra*, *griha*, *riksha*, and *bha* are synonyms denoting the zodiacal signs. Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius are fiery; Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn are earthy; Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius are airy; Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces are watery. 

The lords of the planets from the Sun onwards are the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn; and the preceptors of the gods are Saturn... [The text continues detailing the divisions of *navamsha*, *drekkana*, *hora*, *sapthamsha*, *dwadashamsha*, and *trishamsha* according to classical astrological principles].
pipeline_records.explanation: The text begins with a salutation to Lord Ganesha and an introduction to astrological science, noting that even the wise find it vast. It then explains that the zodiac signs correspond to different parts of the cosmic body, starting with Aries at the head and ending with Pisces at the feet. Additionally, it lists synonyms for zodiac signs, categorizes them by elements (fiery, earthy, airy, and watery), and identifies the planetary lords.
pipeline_records.keywords: Horaśāstra, Bṛhat Jātaka, Jyotiṣa, Zodiacal signs, Navāṃśa, Planetary lords

pipeline_records.ocr_text: यट्प्सप्तसवर्गोहोरैतिलग्नंभवन्नस्त्रचाटूं ९ गोलाश्च्रिकर्किमिथुनाः समृगानि शराब्दाः एषेदया विमिथुनाः कथितास्त एव शीर्षादया दिनवजान्भवंति शेषाः सलग्नंसमेसुभयतः पृथुरोमयुग्मं १० क्रूरः सौम्यः पुरुषवनितेते चराग्दिदेहाः प्रागादीनाः क्रियवृषभ्युत्कर्कटाः सत्रिकोणाः । मार्तेरोऽनैरसुजि युजि भेचन्द्रभावोथ होरेद्रेक्काराः स्युःस्वभवनसुतत्रि त्रिकोणाधिपानां ११ केचित्त्रुहोरां प्रथममाभपस्पवांक्षेति लाभाधिपतेर्द्वितीयां द्वेक्काणासंज्ञामपिवावयंति त्र्यह्रद्वादशेकादशराशियानां १२ अत्रवृषमृगांगनाकुलीलक्षध्वरावोच्यदिवाकरादितंगाः दशशिखिनमुमुक्तिर्थीद्वियांशेस्त्रिनवकविंशतिभिच्वनैस्तनीवाः १३ वर्गोत्तमाश्व्रृगृहादिमुपूर्वमध्यपर्यंनगाः शुभफलानवभागसंज्ञाः सिंहोवृषः प्रथममष्टहृयींग तौलीकुंभास्त्रिकोणाभवानानिभवंतिर्यात् १४ होरादयप्तनुकुटुंबसहृत्यबंधुपुत्रारिपलिमयराणां निथु भास्वदायाः रिफ्कारब्धिसुपचयान्यरिकमेल्यमदुस्त्रिका संक्षितगृहाणिननित्यमेके १५ कल्पस्त्रविक्रम गृहप्रतिभाक्षतानिश्चितित्रायरंध्रगुरूमानभवव्ययानि लाप्ताश्चतुर्थनिधनेचतुरस्रसंज्ञेयुनंचसप्तमगृहद शंशेख्यमाज्ञा १६ कंटककेंद्रचतुष्टयसंज्ञाः सप्तमलग्नचतुर्थख्यानां तेषुयथाविहितेषुवलाढ्यः कीटनरीबुचरः पशवश्च १७ कन्द्रात्परंपराष्परंनश्वसर्वमायोक्रीमंहिवकमेवुमुखंचयेथम त्रमस्त्रभवतं सुतंत्रीकारामैघरंगोदशममत्रचक्रर्मविद्यात् १८ होरास्तामिगुरुसृनवीक्षितयुमाकाज्येश्व
pipeline_records.translation:
When the seven planets move through the signs beginning from Aries, the ascending sign (Lagna) is formed accordingly. The signs Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces are thus designated. Head-rising signs and others are spoken of by the wise. The remaining ones rise differently. Along with the Lagna, both sides (or dual signs) feature the dual fish (Pisces). Crucial and gentle, male and female, movable, fixed, and dual-bodied are the signs governing the east and other directions, starting with Aries, Taurus, and Cancer, along with their triangular counterparts. 

The Sun and Mars rule the odd signs, while Venus and the Moon rule the even signs. Following this are the decans (Drekkanas), belonging to the lords of the same house, fifth, and ninth signs respectively. Some declare the first decan to be of the sign itself, the second belonging to the lord of the eleventh, and so forth. 

The decans of the third, twelfth, and eleventh signs are also spoken of. Here, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, and Cancer are declared as the abodes of the luminaries and others... [text continues with technical astrological divisions of Vargas, Hora, Drekkana, houses, strength, and planetary relationships].
pipeline_records.explanation: This passage lists the twelve zodiac signs starting from Aries and explains how the ascending sign and various types of signs—such as head-rising, male, female, movable, fixed, and dual—are formed and directed. It also states which planets rule odd and even signs and describes how decans (Drekkanas) are assigned to the lords of specific houses.
pipeline_records.keywords: Lagna, Drekkana, Vargas, Rashi, Hora, Planetary strength

pipeline_records.ocr_text: यदाप्तसप्तवर्गो होरेति लग्नं भवत्यचाटूं ९ गोलाश्च्रिकर्किमिथुनाः समुगा निशाः स्युः एते दयाविधिमुनः कथितास्त एव शीर्षादया दिनवजान्भवंति शेषाश्च लग्नसमयेसुभयतः एधुरोमयुग्मं १० क्रूरः सौम्यः पुरुषवणितेतेचराणि देहाः क्रामादीनाः क्रियवृषभयुक्कर्किटाः सत्रिकोणाः। मात्तेरोर्देरखुजियुजि भेवन्दभायेश्वहोरेद्रेक्काणाः स्युःस्वभवनसुतत्रि त्रिकोणाधिपानां ११ केचित्त्रुहोरां प्रथममाभपस्पवांचं छति लाभाधिपतेर्द्वितीयां द्वेक्काणासंज्ञामपिvarयंतिखष्ट्रादश एकादशराशियानां १२ अत्रवृषमृगांगनाकु लीलरूषवरिभोःचदिवाकरादि तुंगाः रणशिखिनमुमुक्तिथितीत्रियांशे न्रिनबविंशतिभिभ्वन्नेस्तनीवाः १३ वर्गोत्तमाश्चरगृहादिमुपूर्वमध्यपर्यन्तगाः शुमफलानवभागसंज्ञाः सिंहोवृषः प्रथममष्टहयी ग तौलीकुंभात्रिकोणाभवनानिभवंतिर्नियात् १४ होरादयलग्नकुटुंवसहत्थयवंधुपुत्रारिपलिमरणानिध्रु भास्परायाः। रिप्फारूढमिसुपचयान्थरिक्मेलंभदुत्रिका संज्ञितगहाणिननित्यमेके १५ कल्सत्वविक्रम गहप्रतिभाक्षतानिवित्रोत्रयरंध्रगुरूमानभवव्यपाति लाप्पादचतुर्थनिधनेचतुरस्त्रसंज्ञेयुनंचसप्तमगृहद शंशेस्त्रमाज्ञा १६ कंटककेंदरचतुष्टयसंज्ञाः सप्तमलगंचतुर्थखभानां तेषुयथाचिहितेषुवलाढ्यः कीटनरंबुचरः पशवश्च १७ कष्ठात्यंपराफपरंस्तरश्चसर्वमायोक्तिमंहिवकमंबुमुखंचयेश्म जामि त्रमस्तभवनेसुतमंत्रिकाणांमेशरेशंदशममंत्रचकर्मविंद्यान् १८ होरास्तामिगुरुज्ञवीक्षितयुमाताभ्येष्य
pipeline_records.translation:
When the sevenfold division (saptavarga) starting with Hora is attained, the ascendant (lagna) is without deceit. The planets residing in Aries, Cancer, and Gemini are nocturnal. These have been declared by the sages of the rules of compassion; those very ones from the head onward belong to day-borns, while the remaining ones at the time of the ascendant on both sides [are also determined]. Leo and Gemini are cruel, while Taurus and Libra are auspicious; these movable signs are bodily. Beginning with Aries, Taurus, and Cancer, along with their trines, they are the bodies of the parts in order. 

The lords of the Hora and Drekkana are respectively of their own houses, sons, and trines, while some desire the first Drekkana of the odd signs to belong to Mars, and the second to the lord of the gains (Jupiter). Others declare the Drekkana designations for the 6th, 8th, and 11th signs. Here, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, and Pisces are the exaltations of the Sun and other planets respectively. 

The planetary parts (navamshas) are located in the first, eighth, and twelfth degrees of the signs, and those called Vargottama reside in the beginning, middle, and end of movable, fixed, and dual signs, yielding auspicious results. Leo, Taurus, the first [part] of Sagittarius, and Aquarius are the trine houses by rule. 

The houses starting from the ascendant represent the body, family, courage, brothers, relatives, children, enemies, spouse, death, fortune, karma, and gains respectively, while the 12th, 8th, and 3rd are places of increase (upachayas). 

Some consider the designated planets to be constantly... The 3rd, 6th, 8th, and 12th houses bring destruction, misfortune, and afflictions. The 4th and 10th are called Chaturasra (squares), and the 7th and the ascendant are the angles (kantas/kendras), also known as Chatustayas. Among them, when duly marked, the powerful ones are centipedes, human-shaped, water-dwellers, quadrupeds... 

One should know the descendant (jatra/astama) as the 7th house, the house of children and mantras [as the 5th], and the 10th as the house of karma (action). The Hora, when aspected by Jupiter and Mercury, together with the Moon, brings forth...
pipeline_records.explanation: The passage describes various astrological rules, including planetary divisions like the saptavarga and drekkana, nocturnal and day-born planets, and the exaltations of the Sun and other planets. It details the specific meanings of the twelve houses—starting with the ascendant representing the body and family, and the 12th, 8th, and 3rd acting as places of increase. Additionally, it lists specific planetary parts, signs, angles, and the directional groupings of powerful signs such as centipedes, human-shaped signs, and quadrupeds.
pipeline_records.keywords: Saptavarga, Hora, Drekkana, Navamsha, Lagna, Vargottama, Upachaya

pipeline_records.ocr_text:
श्रीः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥ श्रीपुरुषोत्तमाय नमः ॥ श्रीकीर्तनाद्यैः ।
वनप्रयेनियम्यसेसारञ्जगटाः उमादिभिषतेभेजरामःसुरर् ।
स्तमः ॥ रागादिरेगानसुतानुषक्रामशेषकायप्रस्तानानेथाक ।
न गैत्सकामोटारतिदानाञ्ज्ञानयोपर्ववैचायनमोम्णतसे ॥
प्रथानप्राग्रूकामीयसप्यायेंबाख्यास्यामः इत्यनत्सलाइराग्रेया ।
ग्रामहर्षयः आयुष्कामायमानेनथमांथसावसाधनम् आयुर्वेदं ।
रोपदेशेषुविधेयःपरमादतः ब्रह्मसरत्वायुधोवेदेप्रजापतिः ।
मञ्जिमदान मोश्विनौतोमस्त्रसांतमोत्रिउडरासिकात्रनीन् ने ।
गिनवेंडिकांतेतएथक्रैवाणितेनिरे तेभ्योतिविश्वकीर्णाभ्यः ।
प्रायःसारतरोरसयः क्रियतेशंगरुदयेनानिसेतिप्रविस्तरत्म् ।
कायबालग्रदोधांगशल्यदंश्रशगजघान ग्रहश्चेगैनितस्याह ।
सिकिसंसोत्तुमेसपिता वायुःपित्तकफभेतिशयोदोषाःसमासतः ॥
pipeline_records.translation:
Om. Salutation to Sri Ganesa. Salutation to Sri Purushottama. Salutation to the holy Kirtana and others. 
[Here follows a corrupted/fragmentary invocation and introductory verse acknowledging deities and teachers.] 
Now, we shall expound the treatise concerning the desire for a long life (Ayurveda), as declared [by the sages]. 
The great sages approached [the teacher] saying: "We desire to know Ayurveda, the means for attaining longevity and righteousness, which is supreme among instructions." 
Prajapati (Brahma) remembered this science of life in its entirety and imparted it to the Ashvins. The Ashvins taught it to Indra, and Indra taught it to Atri and other sages. They, in turn, composed distinct treatises for the benefit of all beings. From those vast and scattered teachings, the essence is extracted and compiled here for the welfare of beings, avoiding unnecessary prolixity. 
[The eight branches of Ayurveda are:] Kayachikitsa (internal medicine), Balachikitsa (pediatrics), Grahatikitsa (psychiatry/demonic afflictions), Urdhvangachikitsa (treatment of diseases above the collarbone/ENT and ophthalmology), Shalyachikitsa (surgery), Damshtra/Agadatan-tram (toxicology), Vrishachikitsa (rejuvenation/aphrodisiacs), and Jarachikitsa (geriatrics). 
In brief, the bodily humors (doshas) are three: Vata (wind), Pitta (bile), and Kapha (phlegm).
pipeline_records.explanation: Sages approached a teacher to learn Ayurveda, the science of longevity and righteousness, which was originally passed from Brahma to the Ashvins, then to Indra, and subsequently to Atri and other sages who wrote treatises. This text extracts the essence of those teachings without unnecessary detail, listing the eight branches of medical treatment. Finally, it states that the three bodily humors in brief are Vata, Pitta, and Kapha.
